fact: The Minister of Digital Economy announced on 9 June 2026 that the first national data centre, run by Gabonese firm ST Digital, would open on 30 June 2026 to keep data from public services and businesses on national territory.

The Presidency states the Head of State said modernising public information systems must guarantee national control and security of the state's strategic data and build national skills to run critical digital infrastructure.

Dcmag reports the Gabonese government signed an agreement on 28 January 2025 with Cybastion for a national data centre, under construction in Libreville, designed to host public administration services and strategic national data and to reduce dependence on foreign infrastructure for hosting national data.
GabonReview reports an ordinance on digitalisation, published in the Journal officiel on 7 September 2025, makes digital sovereignty a priority through control and securing of public data.

Article 27 of Loi N° 027/2023 on cybersecurity and cybercrime (promulgated 11 July 2023, published in Journal Officiel N°218 bis of 15 July 2023) requires data judged confidential or sensitive under its article 22 to be hosted exclusively on national territory, unless the competent administrative authority grants a written derogation.
